masteryZone.q: Which act abolished the dual system of government established by Pitt's India Act?
masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act 1858 ended EIC rule and abolished the double government of Pitt's India Act (Board of Control and Court of Directors).

masteryZone.q: Who was the first Secretary of State for India appointed under the Government of India Act 1858?
masteryZone.sol: Lord Stanley was appointed the first Secretary of State for India in 1858, acting as a member of the British Cabinet with complete authority over Indian administration.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following acts gave statutory recognition to the portfolio system introduced by Lord Canning?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 gave statutory recognition to the portfolio system introduced by Lord Canning in 1859.

masteryZone.q: Under which act was budget discussion allowed in the Legislative Councils for the first time?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 expanded the functions of legislative councils, allowing members to discuss the budget under restrictions.

masteryZone.q: The restoration of legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies under the Act of 1861 marked the reversal of which trend?
masteryZone.sol: It reversed the centralization trend that had peaked with the Charter Act of 1833, initiating the policy of legislative devolution.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following changes were introduced by the Government of India Act 1858? (Select all that apply)
opts: Abolition of the East India Company
Creation of the office of Secretary of State for India
Establishment of a 15-member advisory Council of India
Introduction of direct elections for Central Legislative Council
masteryZone.sol: The 1858 Act terminated EIC rule, created the SoS, and established the 15-member advisory council. It did not introduce elections.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following Indians were nominated to the Legislative Council by Lord Canning in 1862 under the 1861 Act? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Lord Canning nominated the Raja of Benares, the Maharaja of Patiala, and Sir Dinkar Rao. Satyendra Prasad Sinha was nominated in 1909.

masteryZone.q: Under the Indian Councils Act 1892, what new powers or functions were granted to the legislative councils? (Select all that apply)
opts: Power to discuss the annual financial statement (budget)
Power to address questions to the executive under conditions
Power to vote on budget demands and reject them
Power to move resolutions on public interest matters
masteryZone.sol: Members could discuss the budget and ask questions. They did not have the power to vote on the budget or move resolutions (which came in 1909).

masteryZone.q: Which of the following features characterized the Indian Councils Act of 1861? (Select all that apply)
opts: Devolution of legislative powers to Bombay and Madras
Viceroy's power to issue emergency ordinances
Establishment of separate electorates for Muslims
masteryZone.sol: The 1861 Act restored legislative powers, allowed ordinances, and legalized portfolios. Electorates for Muslims came in 1909.

masteryZone.q: Under the Government of India Act 1858, which of the following statements about the Secretary of State for India are correct? (Select all that apply)
opts: He was a member of the British Cabinet
He was directly responsible to the British Parliament
He was assisted by a 15-member advisory Council of India
He was stationed in Calcutta as the head of local administration
masteryZone.sol: The SoS was a British Cabinet minister in London responsible to the British Parliament. The Viceroy was the local head in India.

masteryZone.q: The Government of India Act 1858 declared the British Crown as the direct ruler of India, ending East India Company rule.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Act transferred the governance of India from the Company directly to the British Crown.

masteryZone.q: Lord Canning was designated as the first Viceroy of India under the Government of India Act 1858.
masteryZone.sol: True. Lord Canning became the first Viceroy, serving as the direct representative of the British Crown in India.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 initiated the process of centralization in British India.
masteryZone.sol: False. It initiated decentralization by restoring legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act 1861 allowed the Viceroy to issue emergency ordinances that were valid for up to 1 year.
masteryZone.sol: False. Emergency ordinances issued by the Viceroy were valid for up to 6 months only.

masteryZone.q: Under the Indian Councils Act of 1892, members of the legislative councils could ask supplementary questions.
masteryZone.sol: False. Members could ask questions but could not ask supplementary questions (which was introduced in 1909).

masteryZone.q: The 15-member Council of India established under the 1858 Act was a corporate body capable of suing and being sued in England and India.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Council was constituted as a body corporate for legal purposes, allowing it to sue and be sued.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 explicitly used the word 'election' in its provisions to define how non-official members were selected.
masteryZone.sol: False. The word 'election' was not used; the process was described as nomination on the recommendation of certain bodies.

masteryZone.q: The portfolio system was introduced by Lord Canning in 1859 and received statutory recognition in the Indian Councils Act of 1861.
masteryZone.sol: True. Canning introduced it in 1859 and it was given statutory backing by the 1861 Act.

masteryZone.q: The office of the Secretary of State for India was created by the Government of India Act of ______ (Enter 4-digit year).
masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act 1858 created the office of the Secretary of State for India, assisted by the Council of India.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act of ______ restored legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
masteryZone.sol: The 1861 Act restored legislative powers, reversing the centralization trend of 1833.

masteryZone.q: The validity of an emergency ordinance issued by the Viceroy under the 1861 Act was ______ months.
masteryZone.sol: Ordinances issued during emergencies without legislative council approval were valid for 6 months.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act of ______ allowed the councils to discuss the budget for the first time.
masteryZone.sol: The 1892 reforms allowed budget discussion under specific limitations.

masteryZone.q: The first Viceroy of India under the 1858 Act was Lord ______.
masteryZone.sol: Lord Canning served as the last Governor-General under EIC and the first Viceroy under the Crown.

masteryZone.q: The advisory council consisting of ______ members was established to assist the Secretary of State in 1858.
masteryZone.sol: A 15-member Council of India was established in London as an advisory body to the Secretary of State.

masteryZone.q: Under the Act of 1861, new legislative councils were established in Bengal, North-Western Provinces, and ______.
masteryZone.sol: Legislative councils were set up in Bengal (1862), NWFP (1886), and Punjab (1897).

masteryZone.q: In the 1892 Act, non-official members of the Central Legislative Council were nominated on the recommendation of ______ chamber of commerce and provincial councils.
masteryZone.sol: The Viceroy nominated members on the recommendation of the Bengal Chamber of Commerce and provincial councils.

masteryZone.q: Match the legislative acts of Crown Rule with their key administrative contributions:

options.text: Abolished Double Government & created Secretary of State
Legalized Portfolio System & introduced Ordinance power
Allowed discussion of Budget in Legislative Councils

masteryZone.sol: The 1858 Act abolished double government; the 1861 Act legalized the portfolio system and ordinance-making power; the 1892 Act allowed budget discussion and indirect elections.

masteryZone.q: Match the offices under the Crown administration with their structural descriptions:

options.text: Direct representative of the British Crown in India
British Cabinet Minister with complete authority over India

masteryZone.sol: Viceroy was the direct representative, SoS was a British Cabinet Minister, and the Council of India was a 15-member advisory body.

masteryZone.q: Match the years with the establishment of legislative councils in different provinces:
masteryZone.sol: Legislative councils were established in Bengal (1862), NWFP (1886), and Punjab (1897).

masteryZone.q: Which act redesignated the Governor-General of India as the Viceroy of India?
masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act 1858.

masteryZone.q: Who was the direct representative of the British Crown in India?
masteryZone.sol: The Viceroy of India.

masteryZone.q: In which year was the portfolio system first introduced by Lord Canning in India?
Which act initiated the policy of associating Indians with the law-making process?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Councils Act of 1861.

masteryZone.q: Name one of the three Indians nominated to the Legislative Council by Lord Canning in 1862.
masteryZone.sol: Raja of Benares (or Maharaja of Patiala or Sir Dinkar Rao).

masteryZone.q: Did the Indian Councils Act of 1892 provide for direct elections?
masteryZone.sol: No, it only introduced elements of indirect elections.

masteryZone.q: To whom was the Secretary of State for India responsible for the administration of India?
masteryZone.sol: The British Parliament.

masteryZone.q: What was the maximum validity of emergency ordinances issued by the Viceroy under the Act of 1861?
masteryZone.sol: 6 months.

masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. The 1858 Act ended double government and created the advisory council.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act of 1861:
1. It restored legislative powers to Madras and Bombay.
2. It legalized the portfolio system introduced by Lord Canning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. It restored provincial legislative powers and legalized Canning's portfolio system.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act 1892:
1. It allowed legislative councils to discuss the budget.
2. It permitted members to ask supplementary questions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as supplementary questions were only permitted by the 1909 reforms.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements about the administrative transition in 1858:
1. The Governor-General was redesignated as the Viceroy.
2. The Secretary of State was based in India to supervise the Viceroy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the SoS was based in London, not India.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of legislative councils under the Act of 1861:
1. It required that a majority of the additional members must be non-officials.
2. It associated Indians with law-making by allowing non-official nominations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the act only required that at least half of the additional members be non-officials (not a majority). Statement 2 is correct.

masteryZone.q: Why did the British Crown pass the Government of India Act 1858?
masteryZone.sol: The Act was passed in the wake of the Revolt of 1857 to terminate the dual, inefficient administration of the East India Company and establish direct Crown control, stabilizing the imperial administration.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Indian Councils Act of 1861 considered a major milestone of decentralization?
masteryZone.sol: Because it reversed the centralization policy of the Charter Act of 1833 by restoring legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies, laying down the foundation of legislative devolution.

masteryZone.q: Why did early Indian nationalists criticize the Indian Councils Act of 1892?
masteryZone.sol: Nationalists criticized the 1892 Act because the legislative councils remained powerless advisory bodies. Members could discuss the budget but could not vote on it, ask supplementary questions, or elect representatives directly.

masteryZone.q: How did the Act of 1858 reorganize the executive control of India?
masteryZone.sol: It replaced the Board of Control and Court of Directors with the Secretary of State for India (a British Cabinet member) who operated from London. The Governor-General was redesignated as Viceroy and acted as the local executive head answerable to the SoS.

masteryZone.q: How did the portfolio system change the administration of the Viceroy's Executive Council?
masteryZone.sol: It allowed individual members of the executive council to be placed in charge of specific administrative departments. Each member could issue orders on behalf of the council, replacing collective oversight with individual ministerial responsibility.

masteryZone.q: How did the Indian Councils Act of 1892 introduce election elements without using the word?
masteryZone.sol: It provided that non-official seats in the legislative councils were to be filled by the Viceroy or Governors via nominations based on recommendations from bodies like universities, municipal committees, and chambers of commerce.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Transition from EIC to direct Crown Rule in 1858. Analyze the administrative impact.
masteryZone.sol: The 1858 Act shifted authority from a commercial corporation to a sovereign cabinet. While the 'Act for the Good Government of India' did not change the local rule structure (Viceroy, civil services), it concentrated political authority in London under the SoS. This eliminated the delays of the double government but created an autocratic system entirely unaccountable to the Indian public, prompting future demands for representation.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Devolution of Legislative Powers under the 1861 Act. Examine the shift from centralization.
masteryZone.sol: The Charter Act of 1833 had stripped provinces of lawmaking, centralizing all power in Calcutta. The 1861 Act reversed this by restoring legislative powers to Bombay and Madras and creating councils for NWFP and Punjab. This devolution was vital because a centralized body could not address regional local complexities. However, the councils remained constrained as the Viceroy retained veto and ordinance powers, keeping local self-government subordinate.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Budget Debates of 1892. Evaluate the limits of early financial oversight.
masteryZone.sol: The 1892 Act allowed councils to discuss the annual financial statement (budget). Nationalists like G.K. Gokhale used this platform to expose high military spending and drain of wealth. However, the system was severely restricted: members could not move resolutions, vote on allocations, or ask follow-up questions, meaning the executive could ignore council recommendations without legal consequences.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The Secretary of State for India and the Council of India.
masteryZone.sol: Explain that the SoS was a British Cabinet member in London with supreme authority over Indian administration. To check this authority, the 1858 Act established the Council of India, a 15-member advisory body in London. Most decisions required consultation, but the SoS held veto power on general matters, ensuring imperial control over local colonial administration.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Centralization versus Decentralization in British Indian administration.
masteryZone.sol: Use a flow timeline: (1) Centralization peaked in 1833 when Bombay and Madras lost all legislative powers. (2) Decentralization started in 1861 by restoring these powers. Explain that centralization is efficient for unified military control, while decentralization is necessary for local governance and managing regional diversities.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Direct versus Indirect Election under early British rule.
masteryZone.sol: Explain that direct election involves voters casting ballots directly for candidates. Indirect election (as in 1892) involves voters electing local bodies (like municipal boards), which then recommend representatives to be nominated by the executive. This kept control in the hands of wealthy elites and local authorities.

masteryZone.q: Which act introduced diarchy at the provincial level?
masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced diarchy (rule of two) in the provinces by dividing subjects into Transferred and Reserved.

masteryZone.q: Who was the first Indian appointed as a member of the Viceroy's Executive Council under the Morley-Minto reforms?
masteryZone.sol: Satyendra Prasad Sinha joined the Viceroy's Executive Council as the first Indian Law Member in 1909.

masteryZone.q: Which act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, legalizing communal representation?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

masteryZone.q: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919) introduced bicameralism at which level?
masteryZone.sol: The 1919 Act introduced bicameralism at the Center, replacing the single Central Legislative Council with a Council of State and Legislative Assembly.

masteryZone.q: Under the diarchy system of the 1919 Act, Transferred subjects in provinces were administered by the Governor with the advice of:
masteryZone.sol: Transferred subjects (like education, health) were administered by the Governor advising with ministers responsible to the Legislative Council.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following communities were granted separate electorates under the Government of India Act 1919? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The 1919 Act extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans. Depressed Classes received them under the 1935 Act.

masteryZone.q: Under the Government of India Act 1919, which of the following subjects were classified as 'Transferred' subjects in provinces? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Education and Public Health were Transferred subjects. Land Revenue and Police were Reserved subjects administered by the Governor's Executive Council.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following changes were introduced by the Indian Councils Act of 1909? (Select all that apply)
opts: Increased size of Central Legislative Council from 16 to 60
Allowed members to ask supplementary questions
Allowed members to move resolutions on the budget
masteryZone.sol: The 1909 Act enlarged the council, allowed supplementary questions, and permitted budget resolutions. Diarchy was introduced in 1919.

masteryZone.q: Under the diarchy system of the 1919 Act, which of the following subjects were classified as 'Reserved' subjects? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Finance and Police were Reserved. Agriculture and Local Self-Government were Transferred subjects.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following administrative elements were introduced by the Government of India Act 1919? (Select all that apply)
opts: Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Establishment of a Public Service Commission
masteryZone.sol: The 1919 Act separated provincial budgets, provided for a Public Service Commission (set up in 1926), and central bicameralism. The Federal Court was set up under the 1935 Act.

masteryZone.q: Satyendra Prasad Sinha was appointed as the Law Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council in 1909.
masteryZone.sol: True. He was the first Indian to join the Executive Council, serving as the Law Member under Morley-Minto reforms.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 allowed members of the legislative councils to ask supplementary questions for the first time.
masteryZone.sol: True. The 1909 Act expanded the rules of debate, allowing supplementary questions.

masteryZone.q: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are another name for the Indian Councils Act of 1909.
masteryZone.sol: False. The 1909 reforms are Morley-Minto. Montagu-Chelmsford refers to the 1919 Act reforms.

masteryZone.q: The Government of India Act 1919 established a bicameral central legislature consisting of a Council of State and a Legislative Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: True. It introduced a bicameral structure with elected majorities at the central level.

masteryZone.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced by the Government of India Act of 1919.
masteryZone.sol: False. Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced under the 1909 Act. The 1919 Act only extended them to other groups.

masteryZone.q: The Central Public Service Commission was established in 1926 under the provisions of the Government of India Act 1919.
masteryZone.sol: True. It was set up in 1926 based on the 1919 Act provisions and Lee Commission recommendations.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1919 reforms, provincial budgets were separated from the central budget, allowing provinces to frame their own budgets.
masteryZone.sol: True. The act authorized provincial legislatures to enact their own budgets independently of the center.

masteryZone.q: Voting franchise under the 1919 Act was based on universal adult suffrage, giving all adult Indians the right to vote.
masteryZone.sol: False. The franchise was highly restricted, granted to only 2-3% of the population based on property, tax, and education.

masteryZone.q: Lord ______ was the Viceroy of India when the Indian Councils Act of 1909 was passed.
masteryZone.sol: Lord Minto was the Viceroy, and Lord Morley was the Secretary of State during the 1909 reforms.

masteryZone.q: Lord ______ was the Secretary of State for India when the 1919 reforms were enacted.
masteryZone.sol: Lord Montagu was the SoS, and Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy when the 1919 Act was passed.

masteryZone.q: The 1919 Act introduced diarchy in the provinces, where 'diarchy' is derived from a Greek word meaning ______ rule.
masteryZone.sol: Diarchy comes from the Greek 'di-arche' meaning double rule or dual government.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1909 Reforms, the size of the Central Legislative Council was increased from 16 to ______ members.
masteryZone.sol: The number of additional members in the central council was increased from 16 to 60.

masteryZone.q: The Central Public Service Commission was established in the year ______.
masteryZone.sol: The commission was set up in 1926 to recruit civil servants.

masteryZone.q: The 1919 Act extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Anglo-Indians, Europeans, and ______.
masteryZone.sol: It extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1919 Act, the provincial subjects were divided into Transferred and ______.
masteryZone.sol: Provincial subjects were divided into Transferred and Reserved lists.

masteryZone.q: Satyendra Prasad Sinha was the first Indian to join the Viceroy's ______ Council.
masteryZone.sol: He was the first Indian appointed as the Law Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.

masteryZone.q: Match the legislative reforms with their corresponding historical names:
masteryZone.sol: The 1909 Act is the Morley-Minto reforms; the 1919 Act is the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms.

masteryZone.q: Match the provincial subjects under the 1919 Act with their administrative categories:
masteryZone.sol: Education and health were Transferred; Finance and Police were Reserved subjects.

masteryZone.sol: Lord Minto.

masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act 1919.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act of 1909:
1. It introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
2. It retained an official majority in provincial legislative councils.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because it allowed a non-official majority in provincial legislative councils (retaining official majority at center).

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act 1919:
1. It introduced a bicameral central legislature.
2. It divided provincial subjects into Transferred and Reserved categories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. It introduced diarchy (transferred vs reserved) and central bicameralism.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding separate electorates under Crown Rule:
1. Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced in 1909.
2. The Act of 1919 extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, and Anglo-Indians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. Separate electorates were created in 1909 and expanded to Sikhs, Christians, and Anglo-Indians in 1919.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the division of subjects under the 1919 Reforms:
1. Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with his responsible ministers.
2. Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and his executive council without responsibility to the legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. This is the structural definition of provincial diarchy under the 1919 Act.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding legislative control under the 1919 Reforms:
1. Central and provincial budgets were completely unified under the Viceroy's control.
2. Central control over provinces was relaxed by demarcating central and provincial subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because budgets were separated. Statement 2 is correct.

masteryZone.q: Why did the British colonial administration introduce separate electorates for Muslims in 1909?
masteryZone.sol: The separate electorates were introduced as part of the 'Divide and Rule' policy to separate Muslim voters from the mainstream nationalist movement, preventing a unified Hindu-Muslim national front.

masteryZone.q: Why did the diarchy system fail to work smoothly in the provinces?
masteryZone.sol: Because ministers in charge of Transferred subjects (like health and education) had no control over Finance (which was a Reserved subject). The Governor's executive council had absolute veto power, neutralizing the authority of the responsible ministers.

masteryZone.q: Why was the voting franchise highly restricted under the Government of India Act 1919?
masteryZone.sol: The British restricted the franchise to preserve political control. Only 2 to 3 percent of the population (property holders, tax payers, and university graduates) received voting rights, keeping nationalist majorities small and elite-dominated.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1919 Act structure central bicameralism in British India?
masteryZone.sol: It replaced the single Central Legislative Council with two chambers: (1) The Council of State (Upper House) consisting of 60 members, and (2) The Legislative Assembly (Lower House) consisting of 145 members. Both houses had elected majorities.

masteryZone.q: How did the Indian Councils Act of 1909 associate Indians with executive governance?
masteryZone.sol: It allowed the appointment of Indians to the Executive Councils of the Viceroy and provincial Governors for the first time. Satyendra Prasad Sinha was appointed Law Member of the Viceroy's Council.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1919 Act separate the financial resources of Center and Provinces?
masteryZone.sol: It separated central and provincial budgets. Provincial legislatures were authorized to present and pass their own budgets, ending the dependency on central budget allocations.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Institutionalization of Communalism in 1909. Analyze its impact on Indian unity.
masteryZone.sol: The 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, where only Muslims could vote for Muslim candidates. This communal metrology institutionalized political division. Rather than encouraging a joint electorate, it created communal constituencies. Nationalists argued that this legal communalism led directly to partition, as it incentivized politicians to appeal only to communal interests, weakening the secular nationalist movement.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Working of Diarchy in Madras Presidency (1920-1937). Evaluate the conflict of executive control.
masteryZone.sol: In Madras, the Justice Party took office under Transferred subjects. Ministers faced gridlock: they wanted to reform education and local bodies but lacked independent funds because Finance remained a Reserved subject under the Governor's Executive Council. This case study demonstrates that diarchy split responsibility from authority, creating a system where ministers were blamed for failures while the Governor's executive council held all actual power.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Establishment of the Public Service Commission (1926). Evaluate the indigenization of civil services.
masteryZone.sol: The 1919 Act provided for a Public Service Commission. Following the Lee Commission report, the Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926. This was a major concession to nationalist demands for 'simultaneous examinations' in India and Britain. It institutionalized merit-based civil recruitment locally, paving the way for the post-independence Indian Administrative Service (IAS).

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Separate Electorate vs Joint Electorate.
masteryZone.sol: Explain that in a separate electorate, voters of a specific community (e.g., Muslims) are grouped into a separate constituency and can only vote for candidates of their own community. In a joint electorate, all voters in a geographical area vote together for all candidates, regardless of community (though some seats may be reserved for specific groups like SCs).

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Transferred versus Reserved Subjects under Diarchy.
masteryZone.sol: Use a clear diagrammatic concept: (1) Reserved subjects (Finance, Police, Land Revenue) were critical for imperial control, handled by the Governor and his executive council who were unaccountable to the legislature. (2) Transferred subjects (Education, Health, Agriculture) were welfare-focused, handled by Governor and ministers accountable to the legislature.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Bicameralism and its early structure in India.
masteryZone.sol: Teach that bicameralism is a legislative structure with two chambers. In 1919, the center got: (1) Upper House (Council of State) with a 5-year tenure, representing provinces and elites. (2) Lower House (Legislative Assembly) with a 3-year tenure, representing localized constituencies. This division balanced conservative elite opinion with popular representation.

masteryZone.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, where did the residuary powers lie?
masteryZone.sol: Unlike the post-1950 constitution, residuary powers under the 1935 Act were given to the Governor-General (Viceroy).

masteryZone.q: The Federal Court of India, provided for by the 1935 Act, was established in Delhi in which year?
masteryZone.sol: The Federal Court of India was established in October 1937 with Sir Maurice Gwyer as the first Chief Justice.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following acts abolished the offices of Viceroy of India and Secretary of State for India?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 abolished the offices of Viceroy and SoS, replacing them with dominion status structures.

masteryZone.q: The All-India Federation proposed in the Government of India Act 1935 never materialized because:
opts: Princely states chose not to join
masteryZone.sol: The proposed All-India Federation never came into existence because the princely states refused to sign the Instruments of Accession.

masteryZone.q: Which financial institution was established under the provisions of the Government of India Act 1935?
masteryZone.sol: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established in April 1935 to regulate currency and credit in the country.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following lists were established under the Government of India Act 1935 to distribute legislative subjects? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The 1935 Act divided subjects into Federal List (59 items), Provincial List (54 items), and Concurrent List (36 items).

masteryZone.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, separate electorates were extended to which of the following groups? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Muslims got separate electorates in 1909. The 1935 Act extended them to depressed classes, women, and labor.

masteryZone.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, provincial bicameralism (two chambers) was introduced in which of the following provinces? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Bicameralism was introduced in 6 out of 11 provinces: Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam, and United Provinces. Punjab was unicameral.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following were major provisions of the Indian Independence Act of 1947? (Select all that apply)
opts: Abolition of the office of Viceroy of India
Declaration of Constituent Assemblies as sovereign bodies
Creation of two independent dominions: India and Pakistan
Introduction of provincial diarchy in the dominions
masteryZone.sol: The 1947 Act ended British rule, created India and Pakistan as dominions, and made their assemblies sovereign. Diarchy was not introduced.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following federal institutions were created or provided for under the Government of India Act 1935? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The Federal Court, FPSC, and RBI were established under the 1935 Act. The Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 under the 1919 Act.

masteryZone.q: The All-India Federation proposed in the Government of India Act 1935 was fully functional by 1937.
masteryZone.sol: False. The All-India Federation never came into existence because the princely states refused to join.

masteryZone.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, residuary legislative powers were given to the Federal Legislature.
masteryZone.sol: False. Residuary legislative powers were vested directly in the Governor-General (Viceroy).

masteryZone.q: The Government of India Act 1935 abolished the diarchy system in provinces, replacing it with provincial autonomy.
masteryZone.sol: True. It abolished provincial diarchy and introduced provincial autonomy (responsible government).

masteryZone.q: The Government of India Act 1935 proposed diarchy at the Center, dividing federal subjects into Reserved and Transferred categories.
masteryZone.sol: True. It proposed diarchy at the center, though this part of the act was never implemented.

masteryZone.q: The Government of India Act 1935 abolished the 15-member Council of India that had been established in 1858.
masteryZone.sol: True. It abolished the Council of India, replacing it with a team of advisers to the Secretary of State.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Independence Act 1947 declared the Constituent Assemblies of India and Pakistan as fully sovereign bodies.
masteryZone.sol: True. It gave them full sovereign authority to frame their constitutions and repeal any British act.

masteryZone.q: Under the Indian Independence Act 1947, the British Crown retained the title 'Emperor of India'.
masteryZone.sol: False. The title 'Emperor of India' was dropped from the royal titles of the British Crown.

masteryZone.q: The Federal Court of India established in 1937 was the final court of appeal for British India.
masteryZone.sol: False. Appeals from the Federal Court could still be made to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.

masteryZone.q: The proposed All-India Federation was to consist of British Indian provinces and ______ states.
masteryZone.sol: The Federation was to consist of provinces and those princely states that chose to join.

masteryZone.q: The 1935 Act divided subjects into Federal, Provincial, and ______ lists.
masteryZone.sol: Subjects were divided into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent lists.

masteryZone.q: The Federal Court of India was established in Delhi in the year ______.
masteryZone.sol: The Federal Court was set up in October 1937 under the provisions of the 1935 Act.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1935 Act, the Council of India was abolished and the SoS was given a team of ______.
masteryZone.sol: The 15-member council was abolished, replaced by a smaller team of advisers to the SoS.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Independence Act 1947 ended British rule on August ______, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: The Act declared August 15, 1947, as the official date of independence and partition.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1935 Act, about ______ percent of the total population received voting rights.
masteryZone.sol: It extended the franchise to about 10 percent of the total population.

masteryZone.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in the year ______.
masteryZone.sol: The RBI was established in April 1935 to regulate currency and credit.

masteryZone.q: Under the 1947 Act, the office of the Secretary of State for India was abolished and its functions were transferred to the Secretary of State for ______ Relations.
masteryZone.sol: Residual functions of the SoS were transferred to the SoS for Commonwealth Relations.

masteryZone.q: Match the three legislative lists under the 1935 Act with their respective subject counts:
masteryZone.sol: The Federal List had 59 items, the Provincial List had 54 items, and the Concurrent List had 36 items.

masteryZone.q: Match the acts with their corresponding landmark constitutional contributions:

options.text: Abolished Provincial Diarchy & introduced Provincial Autonomy

masteryZone.sol: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy; the 1947 Act made the Constituent Assemblies sovereign.

masteryZone.q: Match the offices with their changes under the Indian Independence Act 1947:

options.text: Created as nominal constitutional head of each dominion

masteryZone.sol: The Viceroy office was abolished, and the Governor-General of each dominion became a nominal constitutional head.

masteryZone.q: Where did the residuary legislative powers lie under the Government of India Act 1935?
masteryZone.sol: The Governor-General of India.

masteryZone.q: Why did the proposed All-India Federation of the 1935 Act fail to materialize?
masteryZone.sol: Because the princely states chose not to join it.

masteryZone.q: Which act abolished the 15-member Council of India established in 1858?
masteryZone.sol: The Government of India Act 1935.

masteryZone.q: When did the Federal Court of India begin functioning?
Who was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of India?
masteryZone.sol: Sir Maurice Gwyer.

masteryZone.q: Which act granted fully sovereign status to the Constituent Assemblies of India and Pakistan?
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947.

masteryZone.q: What percentage of the total population in India received voting franchise under the 1935 Act?
masteryZone.sol: About 10 percent.

masteryZone.q: Which office was created to manage Commonwealth relations after the SoS office was abolished in 1947?
masteryZone.sol: The Secretary of State for Commonwealth Relations.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both are correct. The 1935 Act provided the legal basis for the establishment in 1937.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the All-India Federation proposed in 1935:
1. It was to consist of provinces and princely states.
2. Joining the federation was compulsory for all princely states.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because joining was voluntary for princely states.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 1935 Reforms:
1. It abolished provincial diarchy and introduced provincial autonomy.
2. It introduced diarchy at the central level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. It abolished provincial diarchy and proposed central diarchy.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding federal institutions under the 1935 Act:
1. The Reserve Bank of India was established in 1935.
2. The Federal Court of India was established in 1937.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. RBI was set up in 1935 and the Federal Court in 1937.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Independence Act 1947:
1. It declared India independent from August 15, 1947.
2. It abolished the office of Governor-General in both dominions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the office of Governor-General was retained as a nominal constitutional head.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding division of subjects under the 1935 Act:
1. The Federal List contained 59 items.
2. The Provincial List contained 54 items.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. Federal list had 59 items, provincial list had 54 items, and concurrent list had 36 items.

masteryZone.q: Why did the 1935 Act propose diarchy at the Center?
masteryZone.sol: To grant limited self-government to Indians while keeping critical matters (Defense, Foreign Affairs, Ecclesiastical, Tribal) reserved under the absolute control of the Governor-General and his advisers.

masteryZone.q: Why did the Indian Independence Act 1947 abolish the office of Viceroy?
masteryZone.sol: Because India and Pakistan became independent sovereign dominions. The office of Viceroy (representing the British Crown's absolute rule) was replaced by nominal Governors-General appointed for each dominion.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Federal Court of India not the final court of appeal?
masteryZone.sol: Because the British Parliament wanted to retain imperial judicial oversight. Appeals from the Federal Court could still be made to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London, which remained the ultimate judicial authority.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1935 Act divide legislative powers between the Center and the Provinces?
masteryZone.sol: It created three legislative lists: (1) Federal List for the center (59 items), (2) Provincial List for provinces (54 items), and (3) Concurrent List for both (36 items). Residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General.

masteryZone.q: How did the 1947 Act govern the dominions before they framed new constitutions?
masteryZone.sol: It provided that both dominions would be governed under the Government of India Act 1935 as a transitional constitution, with necessary adaptations and modifications, until their new constitutions were enacted.

masteryZone.q: How did the Poona Pact of 1932 influence the final electorate provisions of the 1935 Act?
masteryZone.sol: Although the communal award proposed separate electorates for depressed classes, the Poona Pact replaced them with reserved seats within joint electorates. The 1935 Act incorporated these reserved seats and extended separate electorates to women and labor.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Failure of the All-India Federation. Examine the conflict of interest.
masteryZone.sol: The All-India Federation proposed in 1935 was designed to combine democratic British Indian provinces with autocratic princely states. Nationalists opposed it because princely representatives were to be nominated by rulers (not elected by the people). Princely states refused to join because they feared losing their internal autonomy to a democratically-dominated center. Consequently, the federal part of the act was shelved, and the center continued under the 1919 Act structure.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Implementation of Provincial Autonomy (1937-1939). Evaluate its administrative execution.
masteryZone.sol: Provincial Autonomy began in 1937 with elections, leading to Congress ministries in 8 provinces. Governors were expected to act on minister's advice. This worked well for two years, showing that Indian ministers could run complex departments (agriculture, education). However, Governors still held special veto powers to protect minorities and services, showing that autonomy was bounded by imperial safeguards.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Legal Mechanisms of Partition in 1947. Analyze the transfer of sovereignty.
masteryZone.sol: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 was a unique legal instrument. It did not just grant independence; it divided British India. It created two sovereign assemblies, abolished the Crown's suzerainty over princely states (reverting them to independent status), and split the civil services and military. This created a rapid transfer of sovereignty that avoided constitutional vacuum but triggered massive local migration and administrative challenges.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The three legislative lists under the 1935 Act.
masteryZone.sol: Teach the metrology of lists: (1) Federal List had 59 items (e.g., defense, currency, external affairs). (2) Provincial List had 54 items (e.g., police, education, local government). (3) Concurrent List had 36 items (e.g., civil/criminal law, marriage). Contrast this with the modern Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: Dominion Status and Sovereign Constituent Assemblies.
masteryZone.sol: Explain that 'Dominion Status' meant self-governing nations within the British Commonwealth, sharing the British monarch as the nominal head. However, the 1947 Act made their Constituent Assemblies fully sovereign, meaning they could make any laws, draft any constitution, and vote to leave the Commonwealth completely.

masteryZone.q: Teach the Concept: The abolition of the Viceroy and the role of the Dominion Governor-General.
masteryZone.sol: Teach that the Viceroy was a representative of the British Crown's absolute colonial authority. After independence, this office was abolished. The Governor-General of each dominion became a nominal, constitutional head who acted purely on the advice of the dominion cabinet, similar to the modern President of India.
